problem.name: Exact fixed-arity spin optimization
problem.statement_latex:
Given $H(z)=\sum_{S:|S|\le k}J_S\prod_{i\in S}z_i$, output $z^*\in\arg\min H$; $k$ is fixed and coefficients are efficiently represented. QUBO is the case $k=2$ after changing binary variables to spins.
Complexity compares quantum gate time with classical bit time for explicitly represented fixed-arity objective functions.
problem.statement_text: Given $H(z)=\sum_{S:|S|\le k}J_S\prod_{i\in S}z_i$, output $z^*\in\arg\min H$; $k$ is fixed and coefficients are efficiently represented. QUBO is the case $k=2$ after changing binary variables to spins. Complexity compares quantum gate time with classical bit time for explicitly represented fixed-arity objective functions.

quantum.headline_latex: $2^{(1-c_{\rm cl})n/2+o(n)}$, Le Gall--Tamaki quantum conditioning-and-search under the low-energy-density promise.
quantum.headline_text: $2^{(1-c_{\rm cl})n/2+o(n)}$, Le Gall–Tamaki quantum conditioning-and-search under the low-energy-density promise.
quantum.details_latex:
For a centered homogeneous degree-$k$ objective, let $H_{\min}=\min_z H(z)<0$ and suppose
\[
\bigl|\{z:H(z)\le(1-\eta)H_{\min}\}\bigr|\le2^{(1-\gamma)n}.
\]
For fixed $k$, $0<\eta<1$ and $\gamma>0$, the exponent is
\[
c_{\rm cl}=\min\!\left\{\gamma,\ h\!\left(\frac{1-(1-\eta)^{1/k}}{2}\right)\right\},
\]
where $h$ is binary entropy. The algorithm combines amplitude amplification with minimum finding; the weighted formulation removes the known-optimum assumption with a $2^{o(n)}$ overhead. Dalzell et al.'s short-path bound under the corresponding promise has exponent $(1-c_{\rm q})n/2$, where $c_{\rm q}=\gamma\eta/[2(2+\ln2)k]$, for $k\le n/6$ and $\gamma\ge(1+4\log_2n)/n$. The generalized short-path framework gives $O^*(T(n)^{1/2-c(n)})$ for its specified Markov-chain-search cost $T(n)$ under its overlap and spectral hypotheses. The subexponential factors in the conditioning-and-search bounds are displayed explicitly.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{(1-c_{\rm cl})n+o(n)}$ under the same density promise, Le Gall--Tamaki; $\operatorname{poly}(N)2^{O_k(N/\sqrt{\log N})}$ with $N=O_k(n+mb)$, exact threshold counting.
classical.headline_text: $2^{(1-c_{\rm cl})n+o(n)}$ under the same density promise, Le Gall–Tamaki; $\operatorname{poly}(N)2^{O_k(N/\sqrt{\log N})}$ with $N=O_k(n+mb)$, exact threshold counting.
classical.details_latex: The first bound uses the same centered homogeneous objective and parameters as the quantum conditioning-and-search algorithm. For an objective with $m$ integer terms and coefficients of at most $b$ bits, a threshold circuit and its Boolean encoding have $O_k(n+mb)$ variables and gates. Binary search and conditional counting recover an optimum at the displayed counting cost. The classical comparison takes the minimum of the applicable bounds, $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,b)2^n$ enumeration and specialized exact solvers. The density promise, term count and coefficient precision determine which bound is smallest.

strength.description_latex: The paired conditioning-and-search bounds have a quadratic time relationship up to subexponential factors. The overall comparison uses the smallest applicable classical bound. Generalized short paths give a stronger-than-quadratic improvement over their specified Markov-chain-search cost $T(n)$.

evidence.description_latex: The low-energy-density, short-path and exact-counting theorems give rigorous parameter-dependent upper bounds. The paired algorithmic comparison has the same objective and density promise on both sides.

hardware.description_latex:
Fault-tolerant implementation needs $n$ assignment qubits, polynomial reversible workspace and exponentially many coherent operations for the displayed fixed-positive-exponent bound. Cost precision and spectral resolution contribute to depth.

{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the cited CSP comparisons had classical bounds $2^{(1-c\prime)n}$ and quantum bounds $2^{(1-c)n/2}$ for problem-dependent constants, and claimed an improvement in the exponential constant.]\par}
